docs.title: ispra-idrogeo
docs.text:
ispra-idrogeo is a small, typed, async Python library for IdroGEO, the platform where ISPRA (Italy's national environmental agency) publishes what it knows about landslides and floods in Italy. A script can download the national landslide inventory and the hazard maps, keep them up to date, and ask the IdroGEO API for risk figures about any region, province or town. No browser, no copy-pasted links, no account.

async with IdroGEO() as idrogeo:
    folder = await idrogeo.fetch(opendata("frane_piff"))  # 721,365 landslides, one point each

  • Getting started

    Install, download your first layer, look at it, ask the API.

  • Datasets

    Every open-data layer and mosaic, for Italy, a region or a province.

  • AI agents

    idrogeo-mcp: the same data as ten MCP tools for Claude and other agents.

  • Roadmap & AI

    Where the project goes next: improvements and AI features, prioritised.

pip install ispra-idrogeo            # downloads, API, the idrogeo command
pip install "ispra-idrogeo[geo]"     # + GeoDataFrames and GeoParquet
pip install "ispra-idrogeo[mcp]"     # + the MCP server for AI agents

docs.title: What is IdroGEO, in 30 seconds
docs.text:
Italy is one of the European countries most exposed to landslides and floods. For decades, ISPRA and the regions have mapped every landslide they found into one national database, IFFI (Inventario dei Fenomeni Franosi in Italia), and the river basin authorities have drawn hazard maps (the PAI plans) of where the ground may slide and where rivers may flood. ISPRA joins the regional maps into national mosaics, and puts everything on IdroGEO: a web map, open-data files and a public REST API.

flowchart LR
    R["🗺️ Regions and<br/>basin authorities<br/>surveys · PAI plans"] --> I["ISPRA<br/>IFFI inventory<br/>national mosaics"]
    I --> W["IdroGEO<br/>open data (daily ZIPs)<br/>REST API"]
    W -->|ispra-idrogeo| Y["📁 Shapefiles / GeoJSON<br/>on your disk"]
    W -->|ispra-idrogeo| J["🧾 JSON<br/>risk figures, code lists"]
    Y --> U["Your work<br/>GIS · models · dashboards"]
    J --> U

Some of what is in there, straight from the API:

Italy, November 2026 Landslides mapped in IFFI 721,365 Land in high or very high landslide hazard (PAI P3 + P4) 9.5 % of the country, 28,801 km² People living there 1.28 million People living in areas that can flood once in 100–200 years (P2) 6.8 million, 11.5 % of the population Dated landslide events recorded since 2018 1,290

docs.title: What this library does
docs.text:
Feature In plain words 📦 Every open-data file IFFI points, polygons and lines, diffuse-landslide areas, deep-seated deformations, dated events, reports, the two national hazard mosaics, the monitoring readings. 🗺️ Italy or one area The whole country, or one of 19 regions, or a province that publishes on its own (Bolzano, Trento, the Sicilian ones). Shapefile or GeoJSON. 💾 A folder that stays Files go to a persistent folder and are unpacked next to themselves, ready for GeoPandas or QGIS. 🔁 Download once, then only what changed Each file remembers its ETag and Last-Modified. The next run asks "changed?" and gets a 304 for a few hundred bytes. 🛡️ Never half a file Downloads stream to .part and are renamed when complete; ZIPs unpack beside the old folder and are swapped in whole. Memory stays flat even for 1.2 GB. 📊 The REST API Landslide counts and hazard and risk indicators for Italy, macro-regions, regions, provinces, municipalities; every municipality at once, kept on disk; full landslide records; monitoring sites and webcams; code lists; paged searches. 🔄 Retries built in Network errors, 429 and 5xx are retried with exponential backoff. Bring your own httpx.AsyncClient if you want to tune it. 🧪 Pure functions too URL builders, request builders and parsers have no network, for your own HTTP stack.

One dependency: httpx.

docs.title: Who is it for
docs.text:
• Researchers and students in geology, hydrology, civil engineering and remote sensing who want IFFI or PAI in a notebook.
  • GIS analysts and data engineers who keep a copy of the national layers and want it refreshed every night without downloading 3 GB every night.
  • Civil protection, planning and infrastructure teams who need the risk figures of a town, a province or a region, from a script.
  • Journalists and civic-tech projects telling the story of landslides and floods in Italy with numbers you can check.

It started inside Limen, a multi-hazard risk monitor for Italy, where IFFI landslides and PAI hazard are inputs of a landslide-risk model, and was extracted so that anyone can use it.

docs.title: Data licence and credits
docs.text:
Unless stated otherwise, ISPRA publishes its data under CC BY 4.0 (note legali). Anything you publish from it must credit the source, for example:

Source: ISPRA — IdroGEO, Italian landslide inventory (IFFI) and national hazard mosaics.

This library only downloads the data. The figures in this README are drawn from IdroGEO API answers of 3 November 2026 (redraw them with uv run python docs/make_figures.py); the region map is a schematic tile map, not a geographic one.

Code: Apache-2.0. Extracted from Limen.

If this project is useful to you, a ⭐ on GitHub helps others find it.

docs.title: AI agents
docs.text: IdroGEO's data answers questions people actually ask: is my town in a flood zone? How many landslides are there in this valley? Is anyone watching the one above the road? idrogeo-mcp lets an AI agent answer them from the source, with numbers it can cite, instead of from memory.

docs.title: The MCP server
docs.text:
pip install "ispra-idrogeo[mcp]"

idrogeo-mcp is an MCP server, so Claude Desktop, an IDE or your own agent can answer questions like "how many people live in high landslide hazard areas in Sarno, and is anyone monitoring the landslides there?". For Claude Desktop, add it to claude_desktop_config.json:

{
  "mcpServers": {
    "idrogeo": { "command": "idrogeo-mcp" }
  }
}
Tool What the agent gets find_area The ISTAT code of a region, province or municipality from its name area_risk Hazard and exposure: residents, buildings, heritage per hazard class area_landslides IFFI counts by type of movement, events, monitoring landslide One landslide in full, codes decoded search_landslides / search_events Landslides by type and activity; events by area and date monitoring_sites / webcams Who is watching, with which instruments code_list Any code list, in four languages download_dataset A layer downloaded (only if changed) to the local folder

Every tool but download_dataset only reads. Searches stop at limit rows (100 by default, 1,000 at most), so an agent never receives 700,000 landslides at once, and IdroGEO's refusals come back as readable errors.

docs.title: How an agent uses it
docs.text:
A typical question takes three or four tool calls. The agent turns a name into an ISTAT code, then reads the figures for that code:

sequenceDiagram
    autonumber
    participant U as You
    participant A as AI agent
    participant M as idrogeo-mcp
    participant I as IdroGEO API

    U->>A: "How many people live in high landslide hazard in Sarno?"
    A->>M: find_area("Sarno")
    M->>I: list of municipalities (once, then kept)
    M-->>A: [{"code": …, "name": "Sarno", "level": "comuni"}]
    A->>M: area_risk("comuni", code)
    M->>I: PIR indicators of that municipality
    M-->>A: residents per hazard class P1–P4, AA
    A->>M: monitoring_sites(municipality=code)
    M-->>A: sites, instruments, landslides watched
    A-->>U: answer, figures, "Source: ISPRA — IdroGEO"

docs.title: Other clients
docs.text:
The server speaks MCP over stdio, so any MCP client can start it.

Claude CodeClaude DesktopWithout installing (uvx) 
claude mcp add idrogeo -- idrogeo-mcp

{
  "mcpServers": {
    "idrogeo": { "command": "idrogeo-mcp" }
  }
}

{
  "mcpServers": {
    "idrogeo": {
      "command": "uvx",
      "args": ["--from", "ispra-idrogeo[mcp]", "idrogeo-mcp"]
    }
  }
}

docs.title: Questions to try
docs.text:
• Which province of Liguria has the largest share of residents in flood hazard P3?
  • Which landslide monitoring sites are active in the province of Belluno, and with which instruments?
  • Compare landslide hazard exposure (P3 + P4) of Sarno, Ischia and Casamicciola Terme.
  • What do the movement codes 1, 2 and 6 mean, in Italian and in English?
  • Download the Molise landslide points and tell me where the folder is.

Answers are information, not a safety assessment

PAI hazard maps and the IFFI inventory are official, but an agent's summary of them is not. For decisions about a building, a site or an emergency, refer to the competent basin authority, region or civil protection service.

docs.title: For coding assistants: llms.txt
docs.text: This site publishes llms.txt, a short plain-text guide to the library for AI coding assistants: what to call, in which order, and the traps to avoid. Point your assistant at https://agent-engineering-studio.github.io/ispra-idrogeo/llms.txt.

docs.title: Changelog
docs.text: All notable changes to this project are documented here. The format follows Keep a Changelog and the project uses Semantic Versioning.

docs.title: Added
docs.text:
• Documentation site on GitHub Pages (MkDocs Material, API reference from the docstrings), built and deployed by the docs workflow; make docs and make docs-serve. Pages reuse the README sections, so there is one source.
  • A Roadmap & AI page: improvements and AI features, prioritised.
  • llms.txt on the site, for AI coding assistants.

docs.title: Added
docs.text:
• IdroGEO.labels(name, lang) and IdroGEO.code_labels(fields, lang): the API's code lists as {code: label}, in Italian, English, French or German.
  • decode(record, labels): a copy of a record (API, site or shapefile row) with <field>_label next to each coded field; CODE_DICTIONARIES says which code list decodes which field.
  • Extra [geo] (geopandas, pyarrow) and ispra_idrogeo.geo: read opens a downloaded file or folder as a GeoDataFrame, frame turns API rows into one in their own CRS (EPSG:4326 points, EPSG:32632 landslides, EPSG:3857 webcams), add_labels adds <column>_label columns; .to_parquet writes GeoParquet.
  • landslide_filter, event_filter, site_filter: search filters by movement, activity, district, area (ISTAT codes) and dates, in the syntax each search wants.
  • Extra [mcp] and the idrogeo-mcp server (MCP SDK 2.x, stdio): 10 tools for AI agents (find_area, area_risk, area_landslides, landslide, search_landslides, search_events, monitoring_sites, webcams, code_list, download_dataset), codes decoded, answers capped at limit rows.
  • IdroGEO.lookup(kind, text, limit) and idrogeo lookup: text search in the reference lists (geological units, aerial survey flights, bibliography, institutions, professional bodies, funding sources).
  • The idrogeo command: fetch, summary, municipalities, landslides, events, sites, webcams, landslide, labels, dictionaries, lookup; downloads print their path, the rest prints JSON Lines.

docs.title: Fixed
docs.text: • README: the code lists come in four languages, not five.

docs.title: Added
docs.text:
• modified_since on iter_landslides, iter_events and sites: only the records changed since a time-zone-aware datetime, for incremental updates of a local copy (select=["*"] brings the geometry).
  • since_filter(filters, since): the pure filter behind it.

docs.title: Added
docs.text:
• IdroGEO.landslide(id_frana): the full record of a validated IFFI landslide; IdrogeoError for an unknown id (IdroGEO answers 401).
  • IdroGEO.iter_landslides / IdroGEO.iter_events: async iterators over every matching record, page after page, in a stable order.
  • IdroGEO.sites, site(uid), stations(uid): the 1,063 landslide monitoring sites, one site, and its stations with instruments and sensors.
  • IdroGEO.webcams: the webcams pointed at landslides (coordinates in EPSG:3857).

docs.title: Fixed
docs.text:
• Search filters are typed dict[str, Any]: landslide filters take plain values ({"tipo_movimento": 6}), not only strings.
  • parse returns None for a JSON null instead of raising "did not return JSON".

docs.title: Added
docs.text:
• IdroGEO.municipalities(summary="pir") and IdroGEO.summaries(summary, level): the summary of every municipality (7,899), province or region, concurrency calls at a time, saved one JSON per area under <directory>/<summary>_<level>/ and asked again only when older than max_age; an interrupted run resumes.
  • level_codes, CODE_FIELDS, read_json, write_json: the pure pieces behind it.

docs.title: Fixed
docs.text: • README: /api/frana/{id} answers without a login; the detail endpoint that asks for one is /api/evento/{id}.

docs.title: Added
docs.text:
• opendata(layer, area, fmt), mosaic(name), sensor_data(): the IdroGEO open-data downloads (IFFI layers, events, reports, PAI and flood hazard mosaics, monitoring CSV) for Italy or one region or province.
  • IdroGEO.download / IdroGEO.fetch: streamed downloads into a persistent folder (IDROGEO_DATA_DIR), revalidated with ETag / Last-Modified, unpacked atomically.
  • IdroGEO.summary, dictionaries, dictionary, search_landslides, search_events: the public REST API.

docs.title: Contributing
docs.text:
Issues and pull requests are welcome.

  • Run make check before pushing: ruff, mypy --strict and pytest must be clean, the same gate CI runs.
  • Commits follow Conventional Commits.
  • Contributions are accepted under the project's license, Apache-2.0 (section 5 of the license: inbound = outbound). No separate CLA.

docs.title: Ideas to work on
docs.text:
Not promises, just directions where help would make a difference. Open an issue to discuss one before starting. The Roadmap & AI page has the longer analysis, AI features included.

Idea Why it matters Good for 📓 Example notebooks (a town, a valley, a flood plain) Show what the data can do, from download to map first contribution, GIS users 📊 Progress bar for the big downloads (idrogeo fetch) 1.2 GB feels less like a black box first contribution 🗺️ Landslides of an area through the API The search has no reliable area filter today (see the traps); a spatial filter would fill the gap intermediate 🔔 A changes feed: idrogeo watch printing new and changed landslides and events Alerts and dashboards without polling by hand intermediate 🧠 More MCP tools (hazard at a point, nearest landslides) Agents that answer "is my house at risk?" intermediate, AI users 🧩 A GeoServer bootstrap that publishes the downloads, for mcp-geo-server From open data to a live map server in one command advanced 📚 Tutorials on the documentation site Search and API reference are there; step-by-step guides are not yet anyone

Found something odd in IdroGEO? That is a contribution too: open an issue with what you sent and what came back.

See also the Roadmap & AI page for the longer analysis.

docs.title: What you can download
docs.text:
You write What it is Italy, zipped opendata("frane_piff") IFFI landslide identification points, one per landslide 38 MB opendata("frane_poly") IFFI landslide polygons (the outline of each landslide) 573 MB opendata("frane_line") IFFI landslides too narrow for a polygon 18 MB opendata("aree_poly") areas of diffuse landslides (many small ones together) 236 MB opendata("dgpv_poly") deep-seated gravitational slope deformations 4 MB opendata("eventi") dated landslide events (points) 1 MB opendata("segnalazioni") reports small mosaic("pai_frane") PAI landslide hazard mosaic 2020-2021 1.2 GB mosaic("idraulica") flood hazard mosaic 2020 0.75 GB sensor_data() monitoring network readings, CSV (bzip2)

Every opendata layer comes:

  • for Italy (area="ispra", the default), for one region (REGIONS, by ISTAT code: REGIONS[16] == "puglia") or for a province that publishes on its own (PROVINCES: Bolzano, Trento, the nine Sicilian ones);
  • as a shapefile (default) or GeoJSON (fmt="geojson").
opendata("frane_poly", "toscana")  # one region, shapefile
opendata("frane_piff", "trento", "geojson")  # one autonomous province, GeoJSON
opendata("eventi")  # all of Italy

Coordinates are in EPSG:32632 (WGS 84 / UTM 32N), for every area.

docs.title: Where downloads are saved
docs.text:
In a folder that should survive restarts, because the national files weigh hundreds of MB:

  1. the directory you pass to fetch or download;
  2. otherwise IDROGEO_DATA_DIR, if set;
  3. otherwise ~/.cache/ispra-idrogeo (or $XDG_CACHE_HOME/ispra-idrogeo).
~/.cache/ispra-idrogeo/
├── frane_piff_ispra_opendata.zip             # the download, kept to revalidate it
├── frane_piff_ispra_opendata.zip.meta.json   # URL, ETag, Last-Modified
└── frane_piff_ispra_opendata/                # unpacked, ready to read
    ├── frane_piff_opendataPoint.shp
    └── …

In Docker, point it at a volume so the data survives the container:

services:
  app:
    environment:
      IDROGEO_DATA_DIR: /data/idrogeo
    volumes:
      - idrogeo-data:/data/idrogeo
volumes:
  idrogeo-data:

docs.title: 1. Install
docs.text:
pip install ispra-idrogeo            # downloads, API, the idrogeo command
pip install "ispra-idrogeo[geo]"     # + GeoDataFrames and GeoParquet (geopandas, pyarrow)

Python 3.12 or newer. No account and no API key: IdroGEO open data is public.

docs.title: 2. Download your first layer
docs.text:
import asyncio

from ispra_idrogeo import IdroGEO, opendata


async def main() -> None:
    async with IdroGEO() as idrogeo:
        folder = await idrogeo.fetch(opendata("frane_piff", "molise"))
        print(folder)  # ~/.cache/ispra-idrogeo/frane_piff_molise_opendata
        print(sorted(p.name for p in folder.iterdir()))
        # ['frane_piff_opendataPoint.cst', '….dbf', '….prj', '….shp', '….shx']


asyncio.run(main())

That's it: a shapefile with the 23,949 landslides mapped in Molise, one point each. Run it again and it costs one 304 Not Modified.

docs.title: 3. Look at it
docs.text:
With pip install "ispra-idrogeo[geo]" matplotlib:

from ispra_idrogeo.geo import add_labels, read

labels = await idrogeo.code_labels(["tipo_movim"])  # inside the `async with` above
landslides = add_labels(read(folder), labels)  # the folder from step 2
print(landslides.crs)  # EPSG:32632 (WGS 84 / UTM 32N)
print(landslides["tipo_movim_label"].value_counts().head(3))
# slow earth flow                   9168
# complex                           7606
# rotational/translational slide    4279

landslides.plot(column="tipo_movim_label", markersize=1, legend=True, figsize=(10, 8))
landslides.to_parquet("molise.parquet")  # GeoParquet, for DuckDB, QGIS, BigQuery…

Each point carries the landslide's IFFI id (id_frana), its type of movement (tipo_movim, nome_tipo), and the region, province, municipality and river basin district it falls in.

docs.title: 3b. Or from the command line
docs.text:
idrogeo fetch frane_piff --area molise              # prints the unpacked folder
idrogeo summary pir comuni 72006 | jq .popidp2_p    # 1.278
idrogeo municipalities --max-age-days 30 > comuni.jsonl
idrogeo landslides --since 2026-11-01T00:00:00Z --select '*' > changed.jsonl
idrogeo sites --filter stato_monitoraggio=eq.1 --select uid,point
idrogeo labels tipo_movimento --lang it

Downloads print the path they wrote; everything else prints JSON, one object per line for lists (JSON Lines), ready for jq, a file or a database loader. idrogeo --help and idrogeo <command> --help list every option. An error prints one line on stderr and exits with status 1.

docs.title: 4. Ask the API
docs.text:
async with IdroGEO() as idrogeo:
    bari = await idrogeo.summary("pir", "comuni", 72006)  # ISTAT code of Bari
    print(bari["nome"], bari["pop_res021"], bari["popidp2_p"])
    # Bari 315948 1.278  → 1.3 % of residents in flood hazard P2

docs.title: Download once, then only what changed
docs.text:
ISPRA rebuilds the inventory files every day and sends an ETag and a Last-Modified with each one. The library saves them next to the file and sends them back the next time: the server answers 304 Not Modified if the copy you have is still current.

sequenceDiagram
    autonumber
    participant You as Your script
    participant C as IdroGEO client
    participant D as Download folder
    participant S as idrogeo.isprambiente.it

    You->>C: fetch(opendata("frane_poly"))
    C->>D: read frane_poly_….zip.meta.json
    D-->>C: nothing yet
    C->>S: GET /opendata/frane/frane_poly_ispra_opendata.zip
    S-->>C: 200, ~570 MB, ETag "abc", Last-Modified …
    C->>D: stream to .part → rename, save ETag, unpack
    C-->>You: Path to the folder

    Note over You,S: the next day
    You->>C: fetch(opendata("frane_poly"))
    C->>D: read meta.json → ETag "abc"
    C->>S: GET … If-None-Match: "abc"
    S-->>C: 304 Not Modified (no body)
    C-->>You: same folder, nothing downloaded

docs.title: What fetch decides
docs.text:
flowchart TD
    start(["fetch(dataset, directory)"]) --> m{"file and meta.json<br/>on disk, same URL?"}
    m -- no --> g["GET, no conditions"]
    m -- yes --> cg["GET with If-None-Match<br/>and If-Modified-Since"]
    g --> s{"answer"}
    cg --> s
    s -- 304 --> u{"unpacked folder<br/>exists?"}
    s -- 200 --> w["stream to .part → rename<br/>save ETag / Last-Modified"]
    s -- 404 --> e(["IdrogeoError:<br/>layer or area does not exist"])
    s -- "429 / 5xx / network" --> r["wait 2 s, 4 s, 8 s…<br/>and try again"] --> s
    w --> x["unpack into folder.part<br/>swap it in whole"]
    u -- yes --> done(["return the folder"])
    u -- no --> x
    x --> done

A reader never finds half a file or half a shapefile, and a ZIP member that would land outside its folder (../../etc/…) is refused.

docs.title: The building blocks
docs.text:
The library has two layers. Use the high-level client, or call the pure functions with any HTTP library you like.

flowchart LR
    subgraph yours["Your code"]
        H["httpx.AsyncClient<br/>(timeouts, proxy, pooling)"]
    end
    subgraph lib["ispra_idrogeo"]
        direction TB
        CL["client.py<br/>IdroGEO · Download"]
        SO["sources.py<br/>opendata · mosaic · sensor_data<br/>REGIONS · PROVINCES"]
        AP["api.py<br/>summary_path · search_params · parse"]
        CA["cache.py<br/>default_directory · validators · extract"]
        ER["errors.py<br/>IdrogeoError"]
    end
    H --> CL
    CL --> SO
    CL --> AP
    CL --> CA
  • sources.py, api.py: pure functions, no network. They build URLs and requests and read answers. Easy to test, easy to reuse.
  • cache.py: the folder, the .meta.json validators and the safe unpacking.
  • client.py: IdroGEO wires them to your httpx.AsyncClient.

docs.title: Keep a national copy fresh, every night
docs.text:
from ispra_idrogeo import LANDSLIDE_LAYERS, IdroGEO, mosaic, opendata

async with IdroGEO() as idrogeo:
    for layer in LANDSLIDE_LAYERS:
        got = await idrogeo.download(opendata(layer))
        print(layer, "updated" if got.changed else "unchanged")
    for name in ("pai_frane", "idraulica"):
        await idrogeo.fetch(mosaic(name))

The first run downloads about 3 GB. Put it in a cron job: the following runs cost a few kilobytes, plus whatever ISPRA really changed.

docs.title: Only what changed since last time
docs.text:
The nightly download above re-reads a whole file when anything in it changed. To keep your own copy (a database, a GeoParquet file) up to date, ask the API for the records changed since your last run instead:

from datetime import UTC, datetime

from ispra_idrogeo import IdroGEO

since = datetime(2026, 11, 1, tzinfo=UTC)  # saved from your last run
async with IdroGEO() as idrogeo:
    changed = [f async for f in idrogeo.iter_landslides(modified_since=since, select=["*"])]
print(len(changed))  # 20 landslides changed in two days, with their geometry
next_since = max(datetime.fromisoformat(f["modified"]) for f in changed)
  • Save the largest modified you received and pass it next time. The filter is "at or after", so the last record comes back once more: write by id_frana (upsert) and it does no harm.
  • select=["*"] brings every field and the geometry: geom in EPSG:32632, geom_polygon / geom_linestring when there is one, point in lon/lat.
  • iter_events and sites take modified_since too.
  • A removed landslide does not show up as changed: it just stops being listed. Now and then, compare your ids with the full list, one call of about 15 seconds for 721,377 ids:
ids = {f["id_frana"] async for f in idrogeo.iter_landslides(select=["id_frana"], page_size=100_000)}

docs.title: Landslides per region (the map above)
docs.text:
from ispra_idrogeo import IdroGEO

async with IdroGEO() as idrogeo:
    for region in await idrogeo.summary("iffi", "regioni"):
        counts = await idrogeo.summary("iffi", "regioni", region["cod_reg"])
        hazard = await idrogeo.summary("pir", "regioni", region["cod_reg"])
        density = counts["frane_totali"] / hazard["ar_kmq"] * 100
        print(f"{region['nome']:<22} {counts['frane_totali']:>8,}  {density:5.0f} per 100 km²")
# Piemonte                 37,786    149 per 100 km²
# Valle d'Aosta             5,812    178 per 100 km²
# Lombardia               141,970    595 per 100 km²
# …

summary("iffi", …) gives landslide counts (also by type, in frane_stats); summary("pir", …) gives hazard and risk indicators: areas, residents, families, buildings, businesses and cultural heritage in each landslide (*_fr_*) and flood (*_idr_*) hazard class. Levels are "italia", "macroregioni", "regioni", "province" and "comuni", by ISTAT code.

docs.title: Every municipality, in one table
docs.text:
from datetime import timedelta

from ispra_idrogeo import IdroGEO

async with IdroGEO() as idrogeo:
    rows = await idrogeo.municipalities("pir", max_age=timedelta(days=30))
print(len(rows))  # 7899
worst = sorted(rows, key=lambda r: r["pop_fr_p3"] + r["pop_fr_p4"], reverse=True)[:3]
for r in worst:
    print(r["nome"], r["pop_fr_p3"] + r["pop_fr_p4"], f"{r['popfrp3p4p']:.1f} %")
# Napoli 42390 4.6 %     ← residents in landslide hazard P3 + P4, and their share
# Genova 30148 5.4 %
# Sanremo 14607 27.6 %

One call lists the municipalities, then one call each asks for its indicators, 8 at a time: about a minute and 17 MB for all of Italy. Each answer is saved as <directory>/pir_comuni/<ISTAT code>.json, so the next run reads it back from disk (under two seconds), an interrupted run resumes where it stopped, and max_age decides when an answer is old enough to ask again. The indicators come from the 2020-2021 hazard mosaics and the 2021 census, so a monthly refresh is plenty.

municipalities("iffi") does the same with landslide counts, and summaries(summary, "regioni" | "province" | "comuni") with any level.

docs.title: Translate the codes
docs.text:
The data stores codes (tipo_movimento = 4); the API has 73 code lists that say what they mean, in Italian, English, French and German. decode adds a <field>_label next to every coded field it knows:

from ispra_idrogeo import IdroGEO, decode

async with IdroGEO() as idrogeo:
    labels = await idrogeo.code_labels(lang="en")  # one call per code list
    record = decode(await idrogeo.landslide("0017680500"), labels)
print(record["tipo_movimento_label"], "·", record["stato_attivita_1liv_label"])
# rapid debris flow · active/reactivated/suspended

It works on monitoring sites too (strumentazione = [15, 22, 25] becomes ['inclinometer', 'topographic monitoring', 'Satellite SAR interferometry']) and on the rows of a shapefile, where the field is called tipo_movim. CODE_DICTIONARIES lists which code list decodes which field, and labels("cause", "it") gives one code list as {code: label}. A code that is not in its list becomes None rather than a guess.

docs.title: Walk through every landslide or event
docs.text:
from datetime import date

from ispra_idrogeo import IdroGEO, event_filter, landslide_filter

async with IdroGEO() as idrogeo:
    active_sinkholes = landslide_filter(movement=6, activity=100)
    print(len([f async for f in idrogeo.iter_landslides(active_sinkholes)]))  # 217

    tuscany_2023 = event_filter(region=9, start=date(2023, 1, 1), end=date(2024, 1, 1))
    async for event in idrogeo.iter_events(tuscany_2023):  # 8 events
        print(event["uid"], event["computed_date"], event["comune_nome"])

iter_landslides and iter_events ask for one page after another (page_size, 1,000 by default) and stop at the last one. They sort by a unique key (id_frana, uid) so pages do not overlap. An empty filter matches everything; search_landslides and search_events return a single page, if you prefer to page yourself.

landslide_filter, event_filter and site_filter build the filters, because each search reads them its own way: landslides want {"tipo_movimento": 6} but {"stato_attivita_1liv": "eq.100"}, events and sites want operators everywhere, and a range of dates is an "and" of two conditions. Codes are ISTAT codes for areas and the code lists' codes for the rest; a list of codes means "any of these". You can still pass a plain dict if you know the syntax.

docs.title: One landslide, in full
docs.text:
async with IdroGEO() as idrogeo:
    record = await idrogeo.landslide("0017680500")
print(len(record), record["stato"])  # 142 validato_ispra
# activations, causes, state and velocity, damage, interventions, precursors…

The full record of a validated landslide. Many fields are often empty, so check before you rely on them. An unknown id raises IdrogeoError (IdroGEO answers 401 to it, not 404).

docs.title: API rows on a map
docs.text:
frame turns API rows into a GeoDataFrame in the right coordinate system:

from ispra_idrogeo.geo import frame

async with IdroGEO() as idrogeo:
    sites = frame(await idrogeo.sites())  # "point": lon/lat, EPSG:4326
    cams = frame(await idrogeo.webcams(), geometry="geom")  # EPSG:3857, as IdroGEO sends it
    changed = frame(
        [f async for f in idrogeo.iter_landslides(modified_since=since, select=["*"])],
        geometry="geom_polygon",  # or "geom" (point, EPSG:32632), "geom_linestring"
    )

docs.title: Who is watching a landslide: monitoring sites and webcams
docs.text:
async with IdroGEO() as idrogeo:
    active = await idrogeo.sites({"stato_monitoraggio": "eq.1"})
    print(len(active))  # 558 of 1,063 sites are active
    site = active[0]
    print(site["uid"], site["point"], site["id_frane_correlati"])
    # SIABR001 [14.03, 42.24] ['0680013800']   ← lon/lat, and its IFFI landslides
    for station in await idrogeo.stations(site["uid"]):
        print(station["uid"], station["strumentazione"])

    cams = await idrogeo.webcams()  # 14, all in Lombardy

A site is a place where an agency (often an ARPA) monitors a landslide. It has stations, and each station has instruments (inclinometers, piezometers, rain gauges…, decoded by the strumento_monitoraggio dictionary). id_frane_correlati links 880 sites to their IFFI landslides, so you can tell which landslides someone is already watching. Look a site up by its uid ("SIPIE001"), not by its id.

docs.title: Geology, aerial photos, bibliography
docs.text:
async with IdroGEO() as idrogeo:
    units = await idrogeo.lookup("formazioni", "argille", limit=2)
    # [{'sigla': 'AAC', 'nome_unita': 'ARGILLE E ARENARIE GLAUCONITICHE DI CATENANUOVA', …}, …]
    flights = await idrogeo.lookup("voli", "1954")  # [{'id': '0001', 'nome': 'Volo GAI', …}]

The reference lists behind the landslide records, searched by text: geological units (formazioni), aerial survey flights (voli), bibliography (bibliografie), institutions (istituzioni), professional bodies (ordini) and funding sources (finanziamenti). Ten answers by default; limit asks for more. Also idrogeo lookup formazioni argille.

docs.title: For AI agents: the MCP server
docs.text:
pip install "ispra-idrogeo[mcp]"

idrogeo-mcp is an MCP server, so Claude Desktop, an IDE or your own agent can answer questions like "how many people live in high landslide hazard areas in Sarno, and is anyone monitoring the landslides there?". For Claude Desktop, add it to claude_desktop_config.json:

{
  "mcpServers": {
    "idrogeo": { "command": "idrogeo-mcp" }
  }
}
Tool What the agent gets find_area The ISTAT code of a region, province or municipality from its name area_risk Hazard and exposure: residents, buildings, heritage per hazard class area_landslides IFFI counts by type of movement, events, monitoring landslide One landslide in full, codes decoded search_landslides / search_events Landslides by type and activity; events by area and date monitoring_sites / webcams Who is watching, with which instruments code_list Any code list, in four languages download_dataset A layer downloaded (only if changed) to the local folder

Every tool but download_dataset only reads. Searches stop at limit rows (100 by default, 1,000 at most), so an agent never receives 700,000 landslides at once, and IdroGEO's refusals come back as readable errors.

docs.title: Bring your own HTTP client
docs.text:
import httpx

from ispra_idrogeo import IdroGEO

http = httpx.AsyncClient(timeout=httpx.Timeout(30, read=600), proxy="http://proxy:3128")
async with IdroGEO(http, retries=0) as idrogeo:  # your client, your retry policy
    ...
await http.aclose()  # the client is yours: IdroGEO does not close it

docs.title: Handle errors
docs.text:
import httpx

from ispra_idrogeo import IdrogeoError

try:
    folder = await idrogeo.fetch(opendata("frane_piff", "puglia"))
except IdrogeoError as exc:
    # IdroGEO answered, but not with what was asked: 404, API refusal, not JSON.
    print("IdroGEO said no:", exc)
except httpx.HTTPError as exc:
    # Network problems still failing after the retries.
    print("network:", exc)

An unknown layer, area or mosaic name raises ValueError before any request.

docs.title: At a glance
docs.text:
Name What it does IdroGEO(client=None, *, retries=3, backoff_s=2.0) The async client; opens (and closes) its own HTTP client if not given one. .fetch(dataset, directory=None, *, unpack=True) The dataset ready to read: the unpacked folder, or the file. .download(dataset, directory=None) Download(path, changed): the file, and whether this call changed it. .summary(summary, level, code=None) "iffi" counts or "pir" indicators; without code, the list of that level. .dictionaries() / .dictionary(name) The names of the code lists / one list. .landslide(id_frana) The full record of one validated landslide. .iter_landslides(filters, modified_since=, page_size=1000, select=, order="id_frana") Every matching IFFI landslide, page after page; only the changed ones with modified_since. .iter_events(filters, modified_since=, page_size=1000, select=, order="uid") Every matching landslide event, page after page. .sites(filters, modified_since=, select=) The monitoring sites (1,063). .site(uid) / .stations(uid) One site / its stations, instruments and sensors. .webcams(filters) The webcams pointed at landslides. .search_landslides(filters, limit=, offset=, select=, order=) One page of IFFI landslides. .search_events(filters, limit=, offset=, select=, order=) One page of validated landslide events. .municipalities(summary="pir", directory=None, *, concurrency=8, max_age=None) The summary of all 7,899 municipalities, saved one JSON per municipality. .summaries(summary, level, directory=None, *, concurrency=8, max_age=None) The same for every region, province or municipality. opendata(layer, area="ispra", fmt="shapefile") An open-data Dataset (URL + file name). mosaic("pai_frane" \| "idraulica") A national hazard mosaic. sensor_data() The monitoring network readings. REGIONS / PROVINCES / region_area(cod_reg) Area file names by ISTAT code. LANDSLIDE_LAYERS / EVENT_LAYERS / MOSAICS What there is. default_directory() Where downloads go when no directory is given. .lookup(kind, text, limit=10) Search geological units, flights, bibliography, institutions, funding. IdrogeoError IdroGEO answered, but not with what was asked for. .labels(name, lang) / .code_labels(fields, lang) / decode(record, labels) Code lists, and records with <field>_label added. ispra_idrogeo.geo.read(path) A downloaded file or folder as a GeoDataFrame (extra [geo]). ispra_idrogeo.geo.frame(rows, geometry="point") API rows as a GeoDataFrame, in their own CRS. ispra_idrogeo.geo.add_labels(frame, labels) <column>_label columns for coded columns. idrogeo-mcp An MCP server with the same data as 10 tools (extra [mcp]). idrogeo <command> The same from the shell: fetch, summary, municipalities, landslides, events, sites, webcams, landslide, labels, dictionaries.

Lower level, for your own HTTP layer: summary_path, search_params, level_codes, since_filter, parse / parse_list, read_validators / write_validators, read_json / write_json, extract.

iter_landslides(

    order: str = "id_frana",
) -> AsyncIterator[dict[str, Any]]

Every IFFI landslide matching filters, page after page.

docs.title: Sources: what there is to download
sources
docs.text:
Where IdroGEO publishes its open data, as pure URL builders.

The open-data downloads are the ones the IdroGEO web app links to under "Download massivo": /opendata/<group>/<layer>_<area>_opendata.zip, a shapefile, or ….json.zip for GeoJSON. <area> is ispra for the whole of Italy, or the file name of a region or province (:data:REGIONS, :data:PROVINCES). ISPRA regenerates them every day, with an ETag and a Last-Modified, so a conditional GET tells whether anything changed.

The older paths /opendata/iffi/<region>/iffi_<region>_<layer>.zip and /opendata/iffi/dizionari/*.json answer 404 since 2026: the dictionaries are now served by the API (:mod:ispra_idrogeo.api).

Coordinates in the files are in EPSG:32632 (WGS 84 / UTM zone 32N).

docs.title: filters
docs.text:
Search filters without the technical manual.

Each IdroGEO search reads its JSON filter its own way, and the differences fail with cryptic messages. These builders know them (checked on the live service, November 2026):

  • landslides: most fields take operators ("eq.100", "in.(5,6)"), but tipo_movimento takes a plain number and no list. There is no reliable area filter: regione is a relation the search refuses, and regione_2019 is empty for 18% of the landslides (most of Campania). For an area, download opendata(layer, area).
  • events and sites: operators on every field, areas included; a range of dates is an "and" of two conditions.

Every builder returns a plain dict for the filters argument of iter_landslides, iter_events, sites and webcams; combine it with modified_since there.

Codes in the data, and the words they stand for.

IFFI records, the open-data files and the monitoring sites store codes (tipo_movimento = 4); the API's dictionaries (/api/dizionari) say what each code means, in Italian, English, French and German. :data:CODE_DICTIONARIES says which dictionary decodes which field, and :func:decode adds a <field>_label next to each coded field.

An MCP server over IdroGEO, for AI agents: pip install "ispra-idrogeo[mcp]".

docs.title: api
docs.text:
The IdroGEO REST API (/api), as pure request builders and parsers.

Reading needs no account; only writes and a few detail endpoints ask for a login. Summaries and hazard indicators exist for Italy, macro-regions, regions, provinces and municipalities (ISTAT codes); the dictionaries are the code lists the files use (movement types, causes, damage, …).

Searches take a JSON object of filters whose syntax is described in ISPRA's technical manual; an empty object matches everything, so always page with limit and offset.

The query string of a search.

The decoded JSON of a 200; :class:IdrogeoError with the API's message otherwise.

docs.title: cache
docs.text:
The persistent download folder, and what it remembers about each file.

Next to every downloaded file sits <file>.meta.json with the URL and the ETag / Last-Modified the server sent. They become the If-None-Match / If-Modified-Since of the next request, so a file that has not changed is answered 304 and costs no download.

docs.title: Validators dataclass
docs.text: What the server said about the copy on disk.

docs.title: headers
docs.text:
headers() -> dict[str, str]

The conditional-request headers for the next download.

docs.title: default_directory
docs.text:
default_directory() -> Path

Where downloads go when no directory is given.

IDROGEO_DATA_DIR if set, else ispra-idrogeo in the user cache ($XDG_CACHE_HOME, or ~/.cache). Use a folder that survives restarts: the national files weigh hundreds of MB.

docs.title: read_validators
docs.text:
read_validators(path: Path, url: str) -> Validators | None

The validators of a file on disk, or None if it cannot be revalidated.

A file without metadata, with unreadable metadata, or downloaded from another URL is downloaded again rather than trusted.

    path: Path, max_age: timedelta | None = None

A saved API answer, or None if missing, unreadable or older than max_age.

Save data as JSON, atomically: a reader finds the old file or the new one.

docs.title: extract
docs.text:
extract(archive: Path, folder: Path) -> Path

Unpack a ZIP into folder, replacing what was there; folder.

The new content is unpacked beside the old one and swapped in only when complete, so a reader never finds half a shapefile. Members that would land outside folder raise :class:IdrogeoError.

docs.title: Roadmap & AI
docs.text: An analysis of where ispra-idrogeo stands at 0.5.0 (November 2026), and of the improvements and AI features that would make it more useful. These are directions, not promises: open an issue to discuss one before starting.

docs.title: Where we are
docs.text:
Area Today Gap Downloads Every open-data layer and mosaic, conditional GET, atomic swap No progress feedback on the 1.2 GB mosaic REST API Summaries, searches, sites, webcams, code lists, lookups No reliable area filter for landslides (regione_2019 is empty for 18%) and no spatial query at all Geo GeoDataFrames, GeoParquet, labels No local, indexed copy to query: every analysis starts by reading shapefiles AI agents idrogeo-mcp: 10 tools, stdio, decoded codes, row caps Agents cannot answer "is this address at risk?"; no MCP resources or prompts; no remote transport; untyped tool outputs Quality mypy --strict, 100% coverage, mocked transport Nothing notices when ISPRA moves a path again (see Known traps)

The single biggest limit, for people and agents alike, is the missing spatial query. Almost every AI feature below gets better once it exists, so it comes first.

docs.title: 1. A local warehouse
docs.text:
idrogeo sync downloads the layers it is asked for (conditional GET, as today), converts each one to GeoParquet in EPSG:4326 with a bounding-box column, and registers them as views in one DuckDB file with the spatial extension:

idrogeo sync frane_piff frane_poly pai_frane idraulica   # once a night
duckdb ~/.cache/ispra-idrogeo/idrogeo.duckdb

SELECT nome_tipo, count(*) FROM frane_piff
WHERE ST_DWithin(geom, ST_Point(14.62, 40.81), 0.02) GROUP BY 1;

Why it matters: it fixes the "no area filter" trap for good (a spatial join against municipality outlines instead of the half-empty regione_2019), it makes notebooks fast, and it is the ground every AI feature below stands on. New extra [warehouse] (duckdb, pyarrow), so the core keeps one dependency.

docs.title: 2. Point and area queries
docs.text:
await idrogeo.hazard_at(lon=14.62, lat=40.81)
# {"landslide": "P4", "flood": None, "mosaic_date": "2021", "source": "ISPRA — IdroGEO"}
await idrogeo.landslides_near(lon, lat, radius_m=500)
await idrogeo.landslides_in(municipality=istat_code)  # a real spatial join

Backed by the warehouse when present, by the downloaded mosaics otherwise. These are the questions citizens and agents ask most, and today nothing can answer them.

docs.title: 3. Live contract tests
docs.text: The Known traps table was checked by hand on 3 November 2026. A scheduled workflow (pytest -m live, weekly) can check it every week: every path still answers, every field the library reads is still there, the 304 still comes back. On failure it opens an issue. ISPRA changes paths without notice; this is how the library notices first.

docs.title: 4. New tools
docs.text:
Tool Answers hazard_at_point(lon, lat) "Is this place in a landslide or flood hazard zone, and which class?" nearest_landslides(lon, lat, radius_m, limit) "What landslides are mapped near here, which type, are they active?" rank_areas(indicator, level, within, top) "Which ten municipalities of Campania have the most residents in P3 + P4?" — from the municipalities cache, no 7,899 calls compare_areas(codes, indicators) Side-by-side figures, so the agent does not do arithmetic in its head

Turning an address into coordinates (geocoding) should stay outside the server, or behind an explicit, opt-in provider with its usage policy respected: the agent's host usually has a better geocoder already.

docs.title: 5. Resources, prompts, typed outputs, citations
docs.text:
• Resources: the code lists and the dataset catalogue as MCP resources (idrogeo://codes/tipo_movimento), so a client can load them once instead of calling a tool.
  • Prompts: ready-made templates such as risk profile of a municipality or what changed this week in a region.
  • Typed outputs: TypedDict results give each tool an output schema, so agents stop guessing what popidp2_p is. The same types help Python users.
  • Citations: every answer carries source, licence (CC BY 4.0) and retrieved_at, so attribution survives into the agent's final answer.
  • Better find_area: accent- and article-insensitive matching, bilingual names (Bolzano/Bozen), and "did you mean" suggestions.

docs.title: 6. Remote deployment
docs.text: Add idrogeo-mcp --transport streamable-http --port 8000 and publish a container image. Then one shared server, with its download folder on a volume, can serve a whole team or a web app; download_dataset gains a companion, query_dataset, because a local path is of no use to a remote agent.

docs.title: ③ AI features
docs.text:
The design rule for every AI feature here

Numbers come from the data, words from the model. The library assembles the figures deterministically; the model only writes prose around them, and a checker verifies that every number in the text appears in the data. Every output cites ISPRA — IdroGEO and says it is not an official hazard assessment.

docs.title: 7. Agent evaluation suite
docs.text: A set of 50–100 questions ("residents in flood hazard P2 in Bari", "active monitoring sites in Umbria") whose answers are computed from the API, run against an agent connected to idrogeo-mcp. It measures whether the agent picks the right tools, with the right codes, and reports the right numbers. Tool descriptions are prompts: this is how they get tested like code. Runs on demand (it costs model calls), not in every CI build.

docs.title: 8. Grounded area reports
docs.text:
pip install "ispra-idrogeo[ai]"
idrogeo report sarno --lang it --format html > sarno.html

A one-page profile of a municipality: hazard and exposure by class, landslides by type, recent events, monitoring, compared with its province and region. The data part works with no model at all (a template); with an API key, a model writes a plain-language summary for citizens, journalists or council members, in Italian or English. Model-agnostic behind a small interface.

docs.title: 9. Ask the warehouse (text → SQL)
docs.text: An MCP tool and a CLI command, idrogeo ask "…", that turns a question into read-only SQL over the DuckDB warehouse, shows the SQL, runs it, and answers. It covers what fixed tools cannot: "rockfalls within 200 m of a railway in Liguria" once a railway layer is loaded. Guard rails: a read-only connection, a row and time limit, and the schema with code meanings in the prompt.

docs.title: 10. Change digests
docs.text: idrogeo watch polls with modified_since and prints new and changed landslides and events as JSON Lines, to pipe into Slack, a database or a map. On top of it, an optional digest: "This week in Liguria: 14 new events, 9 after the rain of 28 October in the province of Genova…", grounded in the records it lists.

docs.title: 11. For coding assistants
docs.text:
• llms.txt, shipped with this site: the library in one page for AI coding assistants, traps included.
  • An agent skill in the repository (skills/ispra-idrogeo/SKILL.md) that teaches Claude Code and similar tools the recipes: which layer for which question, EPSG:32632 vs 3857, why not to filter landslides by region.

docs.title: 13. A landslide susceptibility baseline
docs.text: A notebook that trains a simple model (gradient boosting) with IFFI landslides as positives and slope, lithology, land cover and rainfall as features, for one region. Useful as teaching material and as a baseline for Limen. Two honest caveats, written into the notebook: IFFI is incomplete where surveys were fewer (sampling bias), and a model is not a substitute for the official PAI hazard maps.

docs.title: 14. News → candidate events
docs.text: A pipeline that reads local news feeds, has a model extract when, where, what type, geocodes it, and matches it to IFFI and IdroGEO events. Output: candidates for review, clearly separated from official data, never written back as if they were ISPRA records.

docs.title: Not AI, still important
docs.text:
• 📊 Progress bar for big downloads (rich or plain \r, off when not a TTY).
  • 📓 Notebooks in the docs: a town, a valley, a flood plain.
  • 🐍 Python 3.14 in the CI matrix.
  • 🧩 GeoServer bootstrap for mcp-geo-server.
  • 🗺️ A static explorer on this site: a nightly workflow writes the 7,899 municipalities' indicators to JSON, and a page shows them on a map with search. No server, no API key.
  • 🏷️ A clear User-Agent with the library's version, and polite default concurrency, so ISPRA can see and reach its users.

docs.title: How to help
docs.text: Pick a row, open an issue saying which one, and read Contributing. Items 3, 5, 11 and 12 are good first contributions; 1 and 2 unlock the rest.

docs.title: Known traps
docs.text:
IdroGEO works well, but its older documentation and many scripts on the web point to paths that no longer exist. This library handles these for you:

You try What actually happens What ispra-idrogeo does /opendata/iffi/<region>/iffi_<region>_<layer>.zip, as in older guides HTTP 404 in 2026: the files moved uses /opendata/frane/<layer>_<area>_opendata.zip the dictionaries in /opendata/iffi/dizionari/*.json HTTP 404: they moved to the API reads /api/dizionari the WFS at geoserver/idrogeo/frane/ows HTTP 401, and the GeoServer lists no layer anonymously uses the open downloads and the API a file for trentino-alto-adige there is none: it publishes per province offers bolzano and trento in PROVINCES downloading the inventory again every day "to be safe" ~870 MB a day, whether anything changed or not conditional GET: one 304 when nothing changed /api/evento/{id}, which the OpenAPI lists with no login HTTP 401 without a login (/api/frana/{id} does answer 200) reads events through search_events, which is public /api/frana/{id} with an id that does not exist HTTP 401 "Missing authorization header", not 404 raises IdrogeoError: unknown or not public /api/sito/{id} with the site's id (a UUID) HTTP 404: the path wants the uid (SIPIE001); /listing of an unknown site answers null with HTTP 200 site(uid) and stations(uid), which raise IdrogeoError for both webcam geom as longitude and latitude it is EPSG:3857 metres, while sites use lon/lat says so in webcams() a webcam's timelapse_url HTTP 404 or a redirect to the web app: the videos are not published leaves the field as IdroGEO sends it {"tipo_movimento": "eq.6"} on landslides, like every other field invalid input syntax for type integer: this one field wants a plain 6, and no list landslide_filter(movement=6) landslides of a region, {"regione": "eq.16"} not an embedded resource; and regione_2019, which does filter, is empty for 18% of the landslides (35,543 in Campania) no area filter for landslides: download opendata(layer, area) several landslides by id, {"id_frana": "in.(…)"} an empty list, no error landslide(id) for each one reading the shapefile while a new version is unpacking half a shapefile, or a crash unpacks beside it and swaps the folder in whole

All checked against the live service on 3 November 2026.
